I mean.. you could maintain a collection of videos (or whatever other content) and keep updating it committing new files without having to reseed a completely new torrent.

Or rename/modify files without having to stop seeding, since it will be a different commit.
(A bit late) Technically you can already do this using BitTorrent Sync.

It wouldn't be the same.

First, Bittorrent Sync is a proprietary technology, vs the open protocol and implementation that Gittorrent offers. I would rather recommend something like Syncthing instead of bitttorrent sync.

Then, sync wouldn't have the same level of flexibility that something like Gittorrent could have.

In Bittorrent sync you just share a vault with other people. Either you give full control to those people (and thus they would be able to manipulate the data, which is not a good idea) or you are the only one in control of the vault (and then if anyone wanted to add some data he would have to create his own vault and start from zero with no seeders).

With Gittorrent there could be multiple versions or forks of the same torrent by different people and still share the seeders from the original commit with the files that are in common. The changes you add on top are added incrementally, without affecting the number of seeders for previous data.
